<p>
        Most agent frameworks today (LangChain, AutoGen, CrewAI, Smolagents, …) optimize for one of two things:
        <strong> "give the LLM tools and a goal, hope it figures it out"</strong>, or
        <strong> "build a complicated DAG of agents"</strong>. Both leak into long-running autonomous work badly:
      </p>

      <ul>
        <li><strong>Tool-loop frameworks</strong> drift on multi-day missions. Context windows fill, attention degrades, the model forgets what was decided three hours ago.</li>
        <li><strong>DAG frameworks</strong> bake too many decisions into code that can't be revised by the agents themselves. Adding a new step requires a developer.</li>
      </ul>

      <p>
        Papercusp takes a third path borrowed from{' '}
        <a href="https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/code-execution-with-mcp" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Anthropic's harness design</a>{' '}
        and{' '}
        <a href="https://www.factory.ai/news/missions-blog" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Factory.ai's missions architecture</a>:
        constrain the loop to a small set of <em>named roles</em>, each invoked with a <em>fresh context</em>,
        each reading state from a structured store and writing decisions back. The roles can't drift because they don't see history;
        they hand off to each other through structured artefacts.
      </p>

      <p>
        That's the substrate. <strong>The Papercusp specification is the open standard for that substrate.</strong>
      </p>

      <div>
        <strong>The pitch in one sentence:</strong> Papercusp is a substrate for running autonomous agent harnesses
        for any long-running mission — coding, research, marketing, ops, anything. The framework is opinionated about
        <em> drift control</em> (fresh contexts, named decisions, file-based handoff). It's <em>unopinionated</em> about
        what mission the harness runs. Anyone publishes a "harness config" via the marketplace; the best ones win.
      </div>

      <p>
        Papercup was a reference install — a 5-director autonomous AI company demo, now preserved-not-active in
        <code>_retired/papercup</code>. It was never the framework's purpose; just an example of what one can ship on top.
      </p>
